_comment: Hand-tune this file freely. Keys are dump categories; values are Vision ClassifyImageRequest identifiers (the exact strings the on-device model returns -- confirmed against the real supportedIdentifiers list via VNClassifyImageRequest.knownClassifications, not guessed). `people` is NOT listed here: it's decided by face detection, never by classification (see CategoryMapper.swift). Anything not listed below, for a photo with zero faces AND no sufficiently confident match in either table, falls through to `detail` -- an intentional, explicit fallback, not a bug. A label only counts if a photo's face count is zero, the label is among its top classifications above ScoringService's own confidence threshold (which just decides what's worth keeping/showing at all), AND its own confidence clears CategoryMapper.categoryMatchConfidenceThreshold (a separate, higher bar for actually accepting a category match -- see that constant's doc comment).
_tuningNote: `place` widened from 50 to 68 identifiers after a real 134-photo device run put only 1 photo in `place` despite the roll containing real scenery. Audited the FULL real taxonomy (1303 identifiers, via VNClassifyImageRequest.knownClassifications) rather than guessing: the original 50 were already 100% real (no typos), but missed a wide swath of common, generic outdoor/scenery vocabulary Vision actually emits -- most notably `outdoor` itself, plus `tree`, `water`, `water_body`, `grass`, `rocks`, `sun`, `cloudy`, `underwater`, `rock_climbing`, `skydiving`, `sunbathing`, `fountain`, `path`, `shore`, `sidewalk`, `statue`, `wetland`. `food`'s one non-real entry (`meal`) was removed -- harmless (silently never matched anything), but dead weight now that the list has been audited against the real taxonomy anyway.
